title: Al-Qadr: the Night of Power
hookLine: angels and the Spirit descend, peace until dawn (Surah 97)

lines: THE LAST TEN NIGHTS OF RAMADAN.
cards: Late in Ramadan, a mosque changes shape. In the last ten nights, the crowds grow. People who work all day come back at midnight and stay until the pre-dawn meal.
Some sleep in the mosque. Children are woken up to join. They're looking for one night, and nobody knows for certain which one it is.
Today's surah is five lines about that night: what it is, why it matters, and how it ends.

teach.h: WE REVEALED IT ON THE NIGHT OF POWER.
teach.b: Surah ninety-seven, in Pickthall's translation: Lo! We revealed it on the Night of Power. Ah, what will convey unto thee what the Night of Power is!
The Night of Power is better than a thousand months.

teach.h: THE ANGELS AND THE SPIRIT DESCEND.
teach.b: The angels and the Spirit descend therein, by the permission of their Lord, with all decrees. The night is Peace until the rising of the dawn. Tradition holds that it's the night the Qur'an was first revealed.
Qadr has two meanings, and scholars keep both: power, honor, greatness; and measure, decree, the night on which matters for the year are measured out.

A thousand months is about eighty-three years: one night, better than a whole life of ordinary nights. The Spirit, ar-ruh, is identified by commentators as the angel Jibril, who brought the revelation.
So the sky that night is full, busy, angels descending. And yet the surah's last word on it isn't noise or power. It's salam.
Peace, until the dawn. When is it?

teach.h: THE ODD NIGHTS OF THE LAST TEN.
teach.b: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said, in Bukhari: seek it in the odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan.
The twenty-seventh is a night people watch especially closely, though scholars say it isn't certain, and some say it moves year to year.
Some see the uncertainty as part of the gift: it keeps people awake for ten nights instead of one.
Aisha asked the Prophet what she should say if she found it, and he taught her a short prayer asking Allah, who loves to pardon, to pardon her.

how: In the last ten nights of Ramadan many Muslims pray late into the night, read Qur'an and make supplication, seeking Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights; some stay in the mosque in retreat (i'tikaf).

o: the new moon that marks the start of Ramadan
the long fast kept on the first day of Ramadan
power and decree, the name of the night of revelation

games.q: what's inside the surah — tap the pairs.

s: everyone knows the Night of Power falls on the 27th
the Prophet said seek it in the odd nights of the last ten; the date isn't certain.
the Night of Power is better than a thousand months
97:3: a thousand months is about eighty-three years.
the surah says the Qur'an was revealed on this night
We revealed it on the Night of Power (97:1).

games.q: Aisha asks the Prophet: if I find the Night of Power, what should I say?
o: ask for wealth for the year
ask Allah, who loves to pardon, to pardon her
games.why: he taught her a short prayer asking for pardon (Tirmidhi). on this night, the request is forgiveness.

practice: This is a small version of waking before dawn and sitting in the dark, no phone: close your eyes or dim the lights, and picture the sky just before sunrise, very still.
Let the word salam, peace, rest on each out-breath, and if you pray, ask for pardon in your own words, as Aisha was taught.

wordCard.voice: Al-Qadr. Power and decree: the night the surah says the Qur'an was revealed, better than a thousand months, peace until dawn. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: peace it is, the opening of 97:5: peace until the rising of the dawn.

carryVoice: Your line: peace until dawn. Ten nights of searching, for one that ends in peace. See you tomorrow.
